title: A Move to Manchester Has Swimmer Ollie Morgan Chasing Medals Again
summary:
Shropshire swimmer Ollie Morgan says moving to Manchester has helped him get back to medal-winning form. The 23-year-old from Bishop's Castle represented Team GB at the 2024 Olympics, breaking a British record on the way to the 100m backstroke final. But he calls this a 'challenging year', with injuries and a change of training base.

The medals tell a happier story. Morgan won five silver medals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow in July, including one in the men's 200m backstroke. Now he is targeting further success at next month's World Aquatics Championships in China, and he sees his switch from Birmingham to Manchester as the key.

'As far as the injuries are concerned, it's just been a question of trying to stay fit,' Morgan said. 'I had a shoulder niggle that wasn't a long-term thing, but took a bit of time to reset.' The move, he said, was meant to push him to another level. 'I'm now training day in, day out with Olympic champions. Racing with them day in, day out has brought the enjoyment back for me. You certainly get found out more.'

One complication is the pool itself. The forthcoming short-course championships will be swum in a 25m pool at the Water Cube in Beijing, rather than the Olympic-sized 50m pools Morgan is used to. 'I've done a lot of work on my starts and turns,' he added, 'which is obviously heavily emphasised in a short-course pool.' His plan is simple: face the hard parts head-on. 'It's about putting yourself in situations you're uncomfortable with. I'm trying to get my weaknesses stronger, so that I can hopefully push for finals and more medals.'
why_it_matters: Morgan's story shows how changing your training environment can bring back the joy in a sport after a hard year. It also shows that top athletes keep working on their weaknesses, like starts and turns, to reach the next level.

Top swimmers train at a base, a pool and coaching centre where they practise every day, and moving base means changing coaches and training partners.

The Commonwealth Games bring together athletes from Commonwealth countries, and the World Aquatics Championships gather the world's best swimmers.
